title: Global AI Laws
subtitle: Every jurisdiction's AI law on its own page, compared
body_html:
This page is the index to the site's AI law pages: one page for each jurisdiction, all built on the same template, with the status of its AI law at a glance, its key instruments, who enforces them, its scope and reach, its obligations, a penalties table taken from the official text, what is coming next, and the date the page was last verified against official sources. The table below is composed from those pages, so it can never say something a country page does not. Only a few jurisdictions have a binding comprehensive AI law in force: the European Union, South Korea and Italy, with China binding through AI-specific rules. Most of the world still governs AI through privacy and sector law, or has a bill or a policy but no act. The EU AI Act is listed first, with its penalties summarised, because it is the most complete binding regime and reaches companies wherever they are based.

The pattern: the binding layer is rarely the AI law

Line the pages up and the pattern holds across continents. A handful of jurisdictions have passed a comprehensive AI act with penalties. A few have AI statutes with no penalties at all, Japan, Taiwan and Peru, which organise government action rather than police businesses. Several have bills or drafts that have not passed. The largest group has no AI act, by choice or by delay, and there the instrument that can fine a company today is the data protection law: UK GDPR, India's DPDP Act, Singapore's PDPA, Saudi Arabia's PDPL, South Africa's POPIA, Nigeria's NDPA and the rest, many of which already restrict decisions made solely by automated processing. A compliance program that waits for an AI act before acting has misread how most of the world governs AI.

How to build one program across these laws: a 5-step path

  1. Map where your AI reaches people, not where you are incorporated. The EU AI Act, South Korea's Framework Act and most privacy laws attach to the people your AI reaches. List every jurisdiction your systems touch and open its page here.
  2. Build on the privacy-law chassis. In most jurisdictions on these pages the instrument that can fine you today is the data protection law. Meet those duties first, including the rules on automated decisions, and add the AI-specific layers on top.
  3. Meet the binding AI acts on their own dates. The EU AI Act, South Korea's Framework Act and Italy's Law 132/2025 apply now, with the EU's high-risk duties deferred to December 2027 and August 2028. Check each page's penalties table and dates.
  4. Use one internal standard for the rest. Where the rules are voluntary, adopt one governance standard, such as ISO/IEC 42001 or Singapore's agentic AI framework, so one set of evidence answers several regimes.
  5. Watch the bills that would change a country's status. Brazil, Chile, Kenya, Nigeria, Indonesia and Thailand have AI bills or drafts in progress, and Australia intends to legislate in early 2027. Each page shows what its regulator and legislature published most recently.

Frequently asked questions about global AI laws

Which countries have binding comprehensive AI laws in force?

The European Union, through the AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; South Korea, through its Framework Act on AI, in force since 22 January 2026; and Italy, whose national AI law, Law No. 132 of 2025, sits alongside the EU Act. China binds through a stack of AI-specific rules rather than one act. Each has its own page, linked in the table above.

Is the EU AI Act a law or a framework?

A law. It is an EU regulation, binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all 27 member states, with fines of up to 35 million euros or 7 percent of worldwide annual turnover. Frameworks and standards such as the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and IEEE 2863 are voluntary and carry no penalties of their own. See the EU AI Act penalties table.

Does no AI act mean no AI obligations?

No. Where there is no AI act, the data protection law, consumer law and sector regulators apply to AI now, and many privacy laws already give people rights over decisions made solely by automated means. The binding layer exists in every jurisdiction on these pages; it is just rarely labelled AI.

How current are these pages?

Each page shows the date it was last verified against official sources: a government, a legislature or an official gazette. Each country's regulator and legislature are watched weekly through their official feeds and index pages, and what the watches find is listed on the country page and on this page. A jurisdiction researched but not yet verified is listed as pending rather than published with facts nobody could check.

citations.quote: Existing governance frameworks such as the NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act articulate essential principles but remain largely static and principle-based, whereas agentic systems are dynamic, tool-using, and adaptive, requiring continuous oversight rather than one-time certification
citations.author: Trustworthy Agentic AI Systems (cross-layer review)

citations.quote: Agent autonomy can be measured directly from the code that governs an agent, allowing autonomy levels to be classified and bounded as a governance control rather than inferred after the fact from behavior
citations.author: Cihon, Schuett & Baum

pending_jurisdictions.name: Vietnam
pending_jurisdictions.reason: A Law on Artificial Intelligence is reported as No. 134/2025/QH15, passed on 10 December 2025 and in force from 1 March 2026, but its text could not be opened: every Vietnamese government site refused the connection.

pending_jurisdictions.name: Kazakhstan
pending_jurisdictions.reason: The President's office confirms that the Law on Artificial Intelligence was signed on 17 November 2025, but its text, number and in-force date could not be opened, because the official legal database refused the connection.

pending_jurisdictions.name: Philippines
pending_jurisdictions.reason: AI bills are pending in the 20th Congress, but only one bill text, S. No. 758 on deepfakes, could be opened; the Senate's records and the official text of the Data Privacy Act answered this crawler 403.

pending_jurisdictions.name: Turkey
pending_jurisdictions.reason: An AI bill is reported in committee at the Grand National Assembly, but every official Turkish site, including the Assembly, the Official Gazette and the data protection authority, refused the connection.

pending_jurisdictions.name: Egypt
pending_jurisdictions.reason: The national AI strategy, the Charter for Responsible AI and the March 2026 national AI governance framework were read on the ICT ministry's site, but no official text of the data protection law's penalties could be found, so a penalties table could not be written from official text.
